pairs.question: Quorum sunt scripta constitutionesque de cultu hortorum?
pairs.derivation: Socrates asks (interrogative quorum) whose writings concern garden-cultivation; Minos answers substantively 'Horticultorum.' Stripped the 'S.'/'M.' speaker labels. Self-contained one-line exchange.

pairs.question: At quorum sunt de condimentis obsoniorum scripta atque instituta?
pairs.derivation: Interrogative (quorum) asking whose are the writings on seasoning of foods; answered substantively 'Coquorum.' Stripped speaker labels; kept the author's connective 'At' as part of the utterance. Self-contained.

pairs.question: Quis spargendorum in terram seminum peritus est?
pairs.derivation: Interrogative (quis) asking who is skilled in sowing seed; answered substantively 'Agricola.' Stripped speaker labels. Self-contained.

pairs.question: Ei vero qui pecudum gregem pascere novit, quod nomen est?
pairs.derivation: Interrogative (quod nomen est) asking the name for one who knows how to feed a flock; answered substantively 'Pastor.' Stripped speaker labels. Self-contained.

pairs.question: An nescis, quae Graecorum gentes antiquissimis legibus utantur?
pairs.answer: Forte Lacaedemonios et Lycurgum Lacaedaemoniorum legum latorem dicis.
pairs.derivation: Socrates asks (interrogative An nescis... quae) which Greek peoples use the most ancient laws; Minos answers substantively naming the Lacedaemonians and Lycurgus. Stripped speaker labels. Self-contained.

pairs.question: Legum earum praecipuae unde venerunt, nosti?
pairs.derivation: Interrogative (unde... nosti) asking where the chief of those laws came from; answered substantively 'Ex Creta ferunt.' Stripped speaker labels and the author's leading connective framing 'sed'; normalized capitalization of the now-initial 'Legum.' Self-contained on the topic of where the laws originate.
